newsitem.title: UK: UK Conservatives challenge Labour on windfall tax.
newsitem.headline: UK Conservatives challenge Labour on windfall tax.

text.p: Britain's Conservatives on Monday called on their Labour rivals to publish the legal opinion they claimed to have showing that their proposed windfall tax on the profits of privatised utilities does not breach British or European law.

Conservative Party chairman Brian Mawhinney said that the legal advice obtained by the right-wing pressure group Aims of Industry that the tax was illegal "opens a new black hole in new Labour's spending commitment".
He said Labour leader Tony Blair had committed a Labour government to an annual 1.8 billion stg of spending to be paid for by the windfall tax on gas, electricity and water firms.
"Without the windfall tax, everybody wants to know where would the money come from," Mawhinney said.
"New Labour refute the findings of this legal opinion by claiming to have one of their own. If this is so they should publish it."
